english.title: Apply for proxy appointment at parliamentary or local election when subject to legal incapacity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you applied for the appointment of a proxy to vote for you at

(A)_[a parliamentary election,]_
(B)_[a local government election,]_
(C)_[parliamentary elections,]_
(D)_[local government elections,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ELECTION OR ELECTIONS..), knowing that

(E)_[you were]_
(F)_[the person to be appointed, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), was]_

subject to a legal incapacity to vote at

(G)_[that election]_
(H)_[elections of that kind]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 61(1)(b) and (7) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
apply for the appointment of a proxy to vote for him
at a parliamentary or local government election or at parliamentary or local government elections
knowing that he or the person to be appointed
is subject to a legal incapacity to vote at the election or, as the case may be, at elections of that kind

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
61(7) An offence under this section shall be an illegal practice but -
(a) the court before whom a person is convicted of any such offence may, if they think it just in the special circumstances of the case, mitigate or entirely remit any incapacity imposed by virtue of section 173; and (b) a candidate shall not be liable, nor shall his election be avoided, for an illegal practice under this section of any agent of his other than an offence under subsection (5) above.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 176

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
